title: Daily reconciliation that only looks bad
prompt: Reconciliation job, every 15 minutes. Average 6 ms elapsed, about 85 logical reads, about 12k rows returned. Actual
plan: Index Seek on IX_Orders_OrderDate (the seek range comes from GetRangeThroughConvert; the index covers
CustomerID, Status and TotalAmount), then a Hash Match (Right Anti Semi Join) against a scan of PK_TestAccounts
(150 rows). No warnings, no spills, estimates within 2x. A static analyzer flagged 'function applied to column in
WHERE' and 'NOT IN with subquery'. The team asks whether to rewrite it.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: AND o.CustomerID NOT IN (SELECT t.CustomerID FROM qe.TestAccounts t);

traps.why: An upper bound of 23:59:59.997 loses rows after .997 on a datetime2(7) column.
example_sql: WHERE o.OrderDate BETWEEN @Day AND CAST(CONVERT(char(10), @Day, 23) + ' 23:59:59.997' AS datetime2(3))
AND o.CustomerID NOT IN (SELECT t.CustomerID FROM qe.TestAccounts t);

traps.why: DATEADD(day, 1, @Day) overflows for @Day = 9999-12-31, where the original returns no rows. It also gives no measurable gain.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case max_day: the baseline returns no rows, the rewrite fails with an overflow error.
example_sql: AND o.CustomerID NOT IN (SELECT t.CustomerID FROM qe.TestAccounts t);

traps.why: Both NOT IN columns are NOT NULL, so NOT IN and NOT EXISTS compile to the same anti semi join. There is nothing to gain.
example_sql: AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qe.TestAccounts t WHERE t.CustomerID = o.CustomerID);

traps.why: A hint on a 6 ms, 85-read query adds compile cost and removes nothing.
example_sql: AND o.CustomerID NOT IN (SELECT t.CustomerID FROM qe.TestAccounts t)

min_improvement.basis: No change is the answer. A candidate is measured only to show that it is not more than 10% worse.

key.reference_notes: Both analyzer flags are false positives here: CAST(datetime2 AS date) still seeks, and NOT IN is safe when neither column can be NULL.
